chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Red Saunders and Jazz Limited with Bill Reinhardt
summary: He visited Saunders's breakfast dances then spent two years at Jazz Limited, playing washboard, singing and drums.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: At this time did you ever go see... Out in Chicago, when you were in Chicago, did you ever go see Red Saunders?

Yes. I used to go down... That's when I was working at the Blue Note. I used to go down and see Red Saunders. But they didn't start a session down there until...I'd say round about... When I'd get through at my

club, I used to go down to Red's... They used to have breakfast dances down at Red Saunders'. [AT THE CLUB DE LISA] I think Red Saunders had an eight-piece band or a nine-piece band. Now, he was a good drummer. Also when I was the second... The first time I was there, at the Blue Note... The second time I went back, I was at the Jazz Limited.

Jazz Limited, yeah. I playing with Reinhardt's... That was 11th Street and... [HESITATES] I can't name the street. I know the number. 111 Grand Street, across the bridge, on the east side. Jazz Limited. I stayed there two years, with Bill Reinhardt and Ruth. Ruth was his wife. She'd take you all to dinner. She'd take care of the band. And after we (?) this place, I got tired and wanted to come back to New York. So I just gave my notice. They said they didn't want me to leave. But I was getting round about...oh, seventy-five dollars, I think I was getting. I was playing washboard, doubling. I was in this show, playing washboard and singing and playing drums. The whole thing was built around me.
